protections: P1: the NNEF .dat reader must bound the header-declared element count and byte counts before allocating or reading - currently `shape.iter().product::<usize>()` with no check (nnef/src/tensors.rs:64), an unchecked bit-size product for bool item_type 5 (:67), and an unchecked byte-size product for plain item types (:78).

P2: for a block-quant .dat header the reader recomputes the blob byte count from the dims and requires it to equal data_size_bytes - `(q_m * q_k) / block_len * block_bytes` with plain arithmetic (nnef/src/tensors.rs:284-287), mirrored by the identical formula in BlockQuantStorage::new (linalg/src/frame/block_quant/storage.rs:20-39).

P3: a .dat tensor bound into an NNEF graph must have the shape the graph declares - enforced by an equality check for plain tensors (nnef/src/ops/nnef/deser.rs:116-122), with no equivalent check for block-quant tensors, which are re-shaped to the graph shape (:105-114).

P4: the shared tensor allocator assumes its caller passes a shape whose product times element size fits usize - `shape.iter().cloned().product::<usize>() * dt.size_of()` (data/src/tensor.rs:282), with the same unchecked product in from_storage (:201) and in the stride/len computation (:552-560).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The `bits_per_item != u32::MAX` skip at :77 looks like exactly the hole the report describes, so the natural hardening makes the byte-size equality unconditional - but tract's own writer emits bits_per_item = u32::MAX for every block-quant tensor (:311) and for String (:219), and :69 deliberately allows one byte of slack for sub-byte bool tensors, so the unconditional rule rejects legitimate inputs.

Block-quant item types 0x2040/0x3040/0x3080 are an internal GGML-style tract extension the NNEF advisory does not name, the reader does not even accept the 0x3081 the writer emits (:315 vs :275-279), and the downstream failure traced here is a bounds-checked slice panic rather than the advisory's OOB read - so the branch reads as out-of-scope draft code.

The shape comes from the graph the user asked to load and `into_tensor_with_shape` is the generic reshaper every exotic tensor uses, while the .dat header was already validated at read time; only the plain-tensor branch performs the shape equality check (:116-122), and nothing re-checks the storage byte count against the graph shape.

This is a different format crate and a different entry point, not the NNEF .dat parser the report names; the unchecked product lives in tract-data's shared allocator used by every op and backend, so it reads as somebody else's layer rather than the parser being fixed.

conflicts.what: The obvious fix for T1 - require `len * (bits_per_item / 8) == data_size_bytes` for every .dat - removes the u32::MAX skip at nnef/src/tensors.rs:77 and so rejects every block-quant tensor tract itself writes (:311) and every 1-bit bool tensor whose payload is ceil(len/8) bytes (the one-byte slack at :69).

Requiring a block-quant .dat payload to match the dense element size (len * 4 for f32) instead of the block formula rejects all valid Q4_0/Q8_1 files, whose payload is 18 or 36 bytes per 32 elements (linalg/src/frame/block_quant/q4_0.rs:182-184, q8_1.rs:169-171) - the same coupled value T2 protects.

The graph shape is deliberately authoritative for block-quant consts because the .dat stores a flattened [m, k] (nnef/src/ops/nnef/deser.rs:105-109); a T3 fix that forces the header shape to equal the graph shape, or that changes the flat-shape convention, breaks legitimate rank>2 models, while a T4 fix must reuse exactly the block_len/block_bytes formula T3 is rewriting.

fairness_risks: Any rule that demands `len * (bits_per_item / 8) == data_size_bytes` for every tensor contradicts tract's own block-quant output (bits_per_item = u32::MAX, nnef/src/tensors.rs:311) and sub-byte bool tensors (data_size_bytes = ceil(len/8), allowed by the one-byte slack at :69).

Any rule that the declared element count times the dense element size must equal data_size_bytes contradicts valid block-quant tensors, whose payload is 18 or 36 bytes per 32 elements rather than len*4 (linalg/src/frame/block_quant/q4_0.rs:182-184, q8_1.rs:169-171).

Rank-0 .dat tensors (empty dims, product 1) and tensors with a zero-length dim (product 0, data_size_bytes 0) are legitimate and must keep loading; a rule that rejects len == 0 or an empty shape breaks them. The bool branch already underflows `real_bit_size - 8` when data_size_bytes is 0 (nnef/src/tensors.rs:69), a debug-build panic adjacent to the check.

The graph shape must remain authoritative for block-quant consts (nnef/src/ops/nnef/deser.rs:105-109); requiring the .dat header shape to equal the graph shape rejects legitimate models where the graph carries the unflattened rank.

The reader and writer block-quant item-type sets already disagree (reader 0x2040/0x3040/0x3080 at nnef/src/tensors.rs:276-278, writer 0x3040/0x3081 at :315); a check added to the branch must keep all three reader types accepted and must not silently change which files load.

A blanket cap on the element count or on individual dims would reject legitimate large multi-gigabyte tensors; the correct bound is arithmetic (no usize overflow, consistent with data_size_bytes), not a magic limit.

design.why: Four independent groups, three of them with a different reason to dismiss. Group 1 (T1+T2) is the reported landing point plus the coupled values a naive hardening breaks: a solver must add checked arithmetic in read_tensor (nnef/src/tensors.rs:64-86) while still accepting the u32::MAX sentinel tract's writer emits for block-quant/String and the one-byte slack for sub-byte bool - this is the mimo (over-hardening) failure and is closed by the same edit as T1, so it counts once. Group 2 (T3) is a second, independent judgement in the same file: read_block_quant_value computes its own blob size with plain arithmetic (:284-287) and is not covered by a fix at :64, with a ready dismiss argument (internal GGML extension, reader/writer item-type disagreement, panic-class rather than OOB impact) - the deepseek 'protection absent plus a reason to dismiss' shape. Group 3 (T4) is a wrong-object trap: for block-quant consts the graph-declared shape silently replaces the header shape with no byte-size check (nnef/src/ops/nnef/deser.rs:105-114 vs the plain-branch check at :116-122), dismissed as generic reshaping - a how-type mechanism mimo tends to miss. Group 4 (T5) is the only extra group on plain storage: the same unchecked product in tract-data's allocator (data/src/tensor.rs:282) reached from the ONNX and TensorFlow raw-tensor deserializers with model-declared dims (onnx/src/tensor.rs:113-134,144-149; tensorflow/src/tensor.rs:86-99), dismissed as a different crate and shared core code. Alternatives considered and rejected: the screener's String .dat route is not real at this commit - read_tensor's String branch calls Tensor::zero_dt (:172), which reaches dispatch_zerolike, has no String arm, and bails (data/src/macros.rs:200-232, bail at :229), so a String .dat never reaches the allocator multiply; the bool item_type 5 branch (:66-69) is not independent either, because once the product at :64 is checked the item-type whitelist (:97-152) rejects every header whose bits_per_item is not 1 or 8, so no overflow survives to allocation. T5 is the weakest member of the design: it is a genuinely exploitable unchecked shape-to-bytes conversion on plain storage, but it sits in other format crates, so hidden tests for it need ONNX/TensorFlow fixtures and must accept that the report never points there.

unverified: The published fix diff is not in this worktree (no fix.diff, no fix commit 34c7df2c present, git history not inspectable with the tools available in this session); the fix's scope and line ranges are taken from the screener record only, so history.a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote are left null.
Nothing was compiled or executed (no shell tool in this session): every reachability claim is from reading the pinned code.

The block-quant residue case (q_m*q_k fits usize but (q_m*q_k)/32*36 wraps to a value equal to a u32 data_size_bytes) was reasoned, not constructed; it needs a search over dims and was not run. Without that wrap the ensure at nnef/src/tensors.rs:287 rejects the header, so the trap is narrow.

Impact class of T3 and T4 was traced to bounds-checked slice indexing (linalg/src/frame/block_quant/storage.rs:72) and to `plain_storage()`'s expect (data/src/tensor.rs:180), i.e. panics rather than OOB reads; whether any consumer reaches as_slice_unchecked over an exotic block-quant tensor with a huge len, or uses BlockQuantFact::buffer_sizes (linalg/src/frame/block_quant/value.rs:45-49, summed into the fact size at core/src/model/fact.rs:272) to under-size a buffer, was not verified.

The safetensors loader (nnef/src/resource.rs:201-217, from_raw_dt at :213) may be another entry into the same allocator, but the safetensors crate source is outside the worktree and I could not check whether it validates shape against data length.

The refutation of the screener's String route (Tensor::zero_dt -> zero_aligned_dt -> dispatch_zerolike has no DatumType::String arm and bails at data/src/macros.rs:229) is from reading only; it was not executed.

The version test at nnef/src/tensors.rs:51 uses `&&` where `||` looks intended, so unsupported versions are accepted; this is an unrelated validation defect, not part of the size-computation family, and was not pursued.

Whether hidden behavioural tests can cover T4/T5 (graph-declared block-quant shape, ONNX/TensorFlow raw tensors) is unknown; both are outside the .dat header the advisory names, and a task built on them would need fixtures those crates' test suites can build.
